label: Road trips
blurb: Scenic drives and classic routes, marked at their best viewpoint.
sources: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime
World's 50 Best road trips (various travel press)

places.name: Pacific Coast Highway at Bixby Bridge
places.why: The single-arch bridge over Bixby Creek is the most photographed frame on the entire Highway 1 run.

places.name: Going-to-the-Sun Road at Logan Pass
places.why: The road's summit, where the Highline Trail sets off and the Garden Wall drops away on both sides.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Icefields Parkway at Peyto Lake
places.why: The overlook above Peyto Lake's fox-head outline is the parkway's defining postcard shot.

places.name: Cabot Trail at the Skyline Trail headland
places.why: The boardwalk loop out to the headland gives the trail's cliff-top sunset view over the Gulf of St. Lawrence.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Blue Ridge Parkway at the Linn Cove Viaduct
places.why: The curved viaduct snaking around Grandfather Mountain's flank is the parkway's engineering icon.

places.name: Route 66 at Cadillac Ranch
places.why: Ten spray-painted Cadillacs nose-down in a field are the road's most photographed roadside stop.

places.name: Overseas Highway at the Seven Mile Bridge
places.why: The old and new bridges running side by side over open water are the drive's signature stretch.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Million Dollar Highway at Red Mountain Pass
places.why: No guardrails and a sheer drop into the red-stained mine tailings make this hairpin summit the drive's icon.

places.name: Beartooth Highway at Beartooth Pass
places.why: Switchbacks climb to nearly 3,340m of alpine plateau dotted with snowfields, the highway's high point.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Trail Ridge Road at Forest Canyon Overlook
places.why: The highest paved through-road in the US tops out here above the treeline with tundra in every direction.

places.name: Hana Highway at Waiʻanapanapa black-sand beach
places.why: After 600-odd curves and 59 bridges, the black volcanic-sand cove at the road's end is the shot everyone stops for.

places.name: 17-Mile Drive at the Lone Cypress
places.why: A single wind-bent cypress on a bare granite outcrop is the toll road's trademark view.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Zion–Mount Carmel Highway at Checkerboard Mesa
places.why: Cross-hatched sandstone right beside the switchbacks and tunnel is the highway's most-shot rock face.

places.name: Death Valley Artist's Drive at Artist's Palette
places.why: Mineral-stained badlands turn pink, green and violet in late light along this one-way loop.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Historic Columbia River Highway at Vista House
places.why: The 1918 rotunda perched on a basalt cliff frames the gorge better than any other stop on the old highway.

places.name: Seward Highway at Beluga Point
places.why: Cook Inlet tide bores and, some days, actual belugas pass right below this cliffside pull-off.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Denali Highway at MacLaren Summit
places.why: The gravel highway's high point looks out over the MacLaren River valley to the Alaska Range with no other traffic in sight.

places.name: Dalton Highway at Atigun Pass
places.why: The only road crossing of the Brooks Range and the highway's most exposed, avalanche-prone stretch.

places.name: Extraterrestrial Highway at the Black Mailbox
places.why: A lone roadside mailbox near Area 51's back gate is the highway's cult photo stop.

places.name: Natchez Trace Parkway at the Double Arch Bridge
places.why: Two 155-foot concrete arches carrying the parkway over a valley form its most photographed span.

places.name: Skyline Drive at Big Meadows Overlook
places.why: A wide meadow break in the ridge gives the drive's classic layered-Blue-Ridge sunset view.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Angeles Crest Highway at Inspiration Point
places.why: A ridge-top pullout above the Mojave-facing slope, the highway's best-known overlook.

places.name: San Juan Skyway at Molas Pass
places.why: The loop's high pass looks straight down into the Animas River valley toward Silverton.

places.name: Moki Dugway above Valley of the Gods
places.why: Three miles of unpaved switchbacks drop 1,100 feet off Cedar Mesa with the valley's buttes spread below.

places.name: Apache Trail at Fish Creek Hill
places.why: A narrow, cliff-hugging grade with a hairpin view down Fish Creek Canyon is the trail's white-knuckle highlight.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Sea-to-Sky Highway at Shannon Falls
places.why: Canada's third-highest waterfall drops right beside the highway under the Stawamus Chief's granite face.

places.name: Alaska Highway at Muncho Lake
places.why: A jade-green glacial lake pressed against the road for miles is the highway's most photographed stretch.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Baja Highway 1 at Bahía Concepción
places.why: Turquoise coves along a 50 km stretch of the Transpeninsular Highway give the drive's best coastline views.

places.name: Copper Canyon Highway at Divisadero
places.why: A rim-edge lookout where the road meets the railway, staring straight into a canyon deeper than the Grand Canyon.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Enchanted Circle at the Wheeler Peak overlook
places.why: The loop's high point looks straight across at New Mexico's tallest summit.

places.name: Talimena Scenic Byway at Rich Mountain
places.why: The byway's highest overlook surveys ridge after ridge of the Ouachitas fading into haze.

places.name: Cherohala Skyway near Huckleberry Knob
places.why: A short trail off the skyway's crest reaches the highest point in the Unicoi Mountains.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Kancamagus Highway at Sugar Hill Overlook
places.region: White Mountain National Forest, New Hampshire
places.why: The highway's best-known pull-off looks down the Swift River valley, unmissable at peak foliage.

places.name: White Rim Road at Green River Overlook
places.why: A sheer 1,200-foot drop to the Green River is the classic first stop on this 4x4 loop below the mesa.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Utah Scenic Byway 12 on the Hogback
places.why: A narrow ridge of road with slickrock falling away on both sides, the byway's most exposed and photographed mile.

places.name: Newfound Gap Road above Cades Cove
places.region: Great Smoky Mountains National Park, Tennessee
places.why: The gap straddling the Tennessee–North Carolina line gives the loop road's signature layered-ridge view.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Klondike Highway above Bennett Lake
places.why: The road crests a pass with the turquoise length of Bennett Lake and old gold-rush rail line below.

places.name: Top of the World Highway
places.why: A ridge-top gravel road runs for miles above the treeline with no valleys, only summits, in view.

places.name: Cassiar Highway at Bear Glacier
places.why: A hanging glacier calving into a milky lake right beside the road, the highway's most photographed stop.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Ruta Panorámica at Cerro de Punta
places.why: Puerto Rico's crest-line highway tops out at the island's highest peak, clouds rolling over both coasts.

places.name: Viking Trail above Western Brook Pond
places.why: A fjord landlocked by ancient uplift is the highway's showpiece, seen from the trailhead pull-off.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Dempster Highway at Tombstone Territorial Park
places.why: Jagged granite peaks rise straight from the tundra at the highway's most-photographed overlook.

places.name: Ruta 40 at the Perito Moreno Glacier balconies
places.why: Boardwalks face the glacier's 60m ice face directly, the single most photographed stop the whole length of Ruta 40.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Carretera Austral at the Marble Caves
places.why: Water-carved calcite caverns on Lake General Carrera, reached by boat from the highway, are the route's icon.

places.name: Yungas Road above Coroico
places.why: A cliffside gravel shelf 600m above the valley floor, still called the World's Most Dangerous Road.

places.name: Salar de Uyuni at Isla Incahuasi
places.why: A cactus-covered coral island rising from the salt flat is the drive's obligatory photo stop and mirror-shot backdrop.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Ruta de los Siete Lagos at Lago Espejo
places.why: A mirror-still lake framed by araucaria forest is the route's most reproduced view between Bariloche and San Martín.

places.name: Quebrada de Humahuaca at the Hill of Seven Colours
places.why: Striated mineral bands stacked above the village are the quebrada's single most photographed backdrop.

places.name: Ruta 52 to Paso de Jama at Salinas Grandes
places.why: A blinding white salt pan crossed by a raised causeway road, just below the high Andean pass.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Transpantaneira Highway at the Rio Pixaim bridge
places.why: One of the road's roughly 120 wooden bridges over the flooded Pantanal, its signature crossing.

places.name: Circuito Chico at Cerro Campanario
places.why: A short chairlift off the road reaches the viewpoint National Geographic once called one of the world's ten best.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Carretera Austral at Cerro Castillo
places.why: A jagged, castle-shaped massif rises straight off the highway's shoulder south of Coyhaique.

places.name: Ruta Nacional 3 at Lago Escondido
places.why: The southernmost stretch of the Pan-American drops through beech forest to this hidden glacial lake before Garibaldi Pass.

places.name: Abra Málaga Pass on the road to Machu Picchu
places.why: Cloud forest gives way to glacier views at 4,300m, the high point of the alternate route into the Sacred Valley.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Colca Canyon road at Cruz del Cóndor
places.why: Andean condors ride the thermals right past this canyon-rim overlook most mornings.

places.name: Quilotoa Loop at the crater rim
places.why: A turquoise crater lake seen from the rim road is the loop's reason for being.

places.name: Ruta 23 at Valle de la Luna
places.why: Wind-carved salt-and-sand formations at sunset are the most photographed stop on the road out of San Pedro.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Trampolín de la Muerte at the Portachuelo summit
places.why: The unpaved road's highest, narrowest cloud-forest saddle between Mocoa and San Francisco, no guardrail in sight.

places.name: Transfăgărășan at Bâlea Lake
places.why: A glacial lake right at the road's summit tunnel is the single image everyone brings back from the Transfăgărășan.

places.name: Transalpina near Obârșia Lotrului
places.why: Romania's highest paved road crosses open alpine plateau here, closed by snow most of the year.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Stelvio Pass hairpins
places.why: 48 numbered switchbacks stacked up the eastern ramp make this the most photographed mountain pass in the Alps.

places.name: Grossglockner High Alpine Road at Edelweißspitze
places.why: A spur to the road's highest viewpoint circles 360° over the Grossglockner and dozens of other 3,000m peaks.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Atlantic Road at the Storseisundet Bridge
places.why: A bridge that seems to launch into open sea is the most photographed structure on any road in Norway.

places.name: Trollstigen at the summit viewing platform
places.why: Eleven hairpins climb below the platform, with the Stigfossen waterfall crashing beside the road.

places.name: Lofoten road at Reinebringen
places.why: The switchback climb above Reine gives Lofoten's most reproduced view: a fishing village pinched between fjord and peaks.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: North Coast 500 at Bealach na Bà
places.why: Scotland's steepest ascent, a single-track pass to a Skye-facing summit, is the loop's toughest and most-shot stretch.

places.name: Wild Atlantic Way at the Cliffs of Moher
places.why: 214m sea cliffs facing the open Atlantic are the single most-visited and most-photographed stop on the whole route.

places.name: Ring of Kerry at Ladies' View
places.why: Named for Queen Victoria's ladies-in-waiting, this pull-off over the lakes of Killarney is the ring's classic stop.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Amalfi Coast Road below the Path of the Gods
places.why: The cliffside trail above the SS163 frames Positano and the coast road stacked below in the classic Amalfi shot.

places.name: Great Dolomites Road at Passo Pordoi
places.why: A cable car and a wall of Sella massif rock make this the Dolomites Road's best-known summit.

places.name: Sella Ronda at Passo Sella
places.why: Sheer dolomite towers rise on both sides of the pass, the loop's most-photographed saddle.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Furka Pass hairpins
places.why: The stacked switchbacks below the summit, familiar from a James Bond car chase, are the pass's signature view.

places.name: Grimsel Pass summit
places.why: Bare granite and glacial lakes surround the road at its highest point between the Bernese Oberland and Valais.

places.name: Route des Grandes Alpes at Col de la Bonette
places.why: A loop road around the summit makes this one of the highest paved points in Europe, moon-like scree on all sides.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Col du Tourmalet summit
places.why: A cyclist statue marks the Tour de France's most-climbed pass, its hairpins visible for miles below.

places.name: Route des Crêtes at Point Sublime
places.why: The corniche road's best-named overlook drops 180m straight into Europe's grandest canyon.

places.name: Golden Circle at Gullfoss
places.why: A two-tiered waterfall dropping into a hidden canyon is the loop's most-shot stop.

places.name: Iceland Ring Road at Diamond Beach
places.why: Glacier ice washes up and glitters on black volcanic sand right beside Route 1 — the Ring Road's single most-photographed stop.

places.name: Causeway Coastal Route at the Giant's Causeway
places.why: 40,000 hexagonal basalt columns make this the route's UNESCO-listed centrepiece.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Sa Calobra Road at Mirador de Ses Barques
places.why: A 270° hairpin loop and a sheer drop to the Mediterranean make this the road's most-shot bend.

places.name: Route Napoléon at the Sisteron gorge
places.why: A citadel-topped rock gate squeezing the Durance river is the route's most dramatic pinch point.

places.name: Timmelsjoch High Alpine Road summit
places.why: A striking angular museum building marks the Austria–Italy border crossing at the road's highest point.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Sognefjellsvegen summit
places.why: Northern Europe's highest mountain road crosses a glacier-studded plateau at over 1,400m.

places.name: Rv7 across Hardangervidda at Møsvatn
places.why: Europe's largest mountain plateau stretches flat and treeless in every direction from this stretch of road.

places.name: Lysebotn Road below Kjeragbolten
places.why: 27 hairpins and a tunnel spiral down to the fjord floor beneath the famous wedged boulder.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Route des Crêtes de Corse at Col de Bavella
places.why: Granite needles called the Aiguilles de Bavella rise straight above the pass, Corsica's most-shot mountain road view.

places.name: Passo Gavia summit
places.why: A narrow, largely unguarded single-lane road tops out beside a small alpine lake below Punta di San Matteo.

places.name: Vršič Pass summit
places.why: 50 hairpins, several still cobbled, climb to Slovenia's highest road pass beneath the Julian Alps.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: A82 through Glencoe at Buachaille Etive Mòr
places.why: The pyramidal peak beside the road, framed by the River Coupall, is the most-photographed shot in the Highlands.

places.name: Peak District Snake Pass road at Mam Tor
places.why: A ridge-top car park below Mam Tor gives the classic view down the Hope and Edale valleys.

places.name: N222 above the Douro Valley
places.why: Terraced vineyards stacked above the river bend are the reason Top Gear once called this the world's best road.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Serranía de Ronda road at the Puente Nuevo
places.why: An 18th-century bridge spanning a 120m gorge splits the town in two, the drive's dramatic centrepiece.

places.name: Picos de Europa road at Fuente Dé
places.why: A cable car climbs 800m from the road's end into a sheer limestone amphitheatre.

places.name: Romantische Straße at the Marienbrücke
places.why: A footbridge over the Pöllat gorge gives the classic postcard view of Neuschwanstein Castle beside the road.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Schwarzwaldhochstraße at the Mummelsee
places.why: A dark glacial lake ringed by spruce right beside the high road is the route's best-known stop.

places.name: Westfjords Way at Dynjandi
places.why: A tiered, fan-shaped waterfall visible from the gravel road is the Westfjords loop's must-stop.

places.name: Adriatic Highway above Dubrovnik
places.why: A hillside pull-off on the coastal D8 gives the classic elevated view of the old town's red roofs and walls.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Kotor Serpentine Road summit
places.why: 25 numbered switchbacks climb from the bay, with a fjord-like panorama at the top hairpin.

places.name: Meteora monastery road viewpoint
places.why: Sandstone pillars topped with centuries-old monasteries line the loop road above Kalambaka.

places.name: Faroe Islands road to Múlafossur
places.why: A waterfall dropping straight into the Atlantic beside the village is the islands' single most-shot frame.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Isle of Skye road below the Quiraing
places.why: A landslipped ridge of pinnacles and hidden plateaus makes the road below it Skye's most-photographed corner.

places.name: Snowdonia road through Llanberis Pass
places.why: Boulder-strewn slopes squeeze the road between Snowdon and the Glyderau, Wales's classic mountain drive.

places.name: Pyrenees road to the Cirque de Gavarnie
places.why: A natural amphitheatre of cliffs and waterfalls at the road's end, the Pyrenees' most famous view.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Klausenpass summit
places.why: A quieter alternative to the Alps' famous passes, with the Clariden glacier in view from the top.

places.name: Sustenpass at the Steingletscher viewpoint
places.why: A roadside glacier lake and hanging ice tongue make this the pass's most-photographed pull-off.

places.name: Silvretta Hochalpenstraße at Bielerhöhe
places.why: A dammed alpine reservoir at the road's summit is the Silvretta road's classic reflective shot.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Corniche de l'Estérel at Cap Roux
places.why: Red volcanic rock plunging into blue sea is the corniche's most vivid stretch, best just after sunrise.

places.name: Route Blanche at Col des Montets
places.why: Mont Blanc's glaciers dominate the skyline from this pass linking Chamonix to Switzerland.

places.name: SS340 above Lake Como at Bellagio
places.why: The road's lakeside curves frame the promontory town where Como's two branches meet.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: SS114 at Taormina overlooking Etna
places.why: A clifftop Greek theatre and smoking Etna in the same frame make this the coast road's icon.

places.name: SP71 along the Costa Smeralda
places.why: Granite headlands and turquoise coves line this coastal stretch north of Olbia.

places.name: CG2 at the Port d'Envalira
places.why: The Pyrenees' highest paved pass, linking Andorra to France, tops out above the treeline.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Garden Route at the Storms River suspension bridge
places.why: A swaying footbridge over a gorge mouth into the Indian Ocean is the route's best-known stop.

places.name: Chapman's Peak Drive viewpoint
places.why: 114 curves carved into a sheer cliff give unbroken views over Hout Bay from almost every bend.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Sani Pass summit
places.why: A gravel switchback climb to Africa's highest border post, snowed in some winters, its trademark hairpins visible below.

places.name: N7 Namaqualand at Skilpad Wildflower Reserve
places.why: For a few weeks each spring the roadside desert turns solid orange with daisies.

places.name: Tizi n'Tichka Pass summit
places.why: The highest paved pass in North Africa switchbacks over the Atlas between Marrakech and Ouarzazate.

places.name: Road of a Thousand Kasbahs at the Dades Gorge
places.why: Hairpins stacked against red rock walls above the Dades River are the road's signature switchback view.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Skeleton Coast Road at Cape Cross
places.why: Fog rolls off the cold Atlantic over one of the coast's oldest landmarks and a huge Cape fur seal colony.

places.name: Namibia's C33 at Spitzkoppe
places.why: A granite inselberg rising sheer from flat desert is Namibia's most-photographed roadside stop.

places.name: A8 at the Victoria Falls Bridge
places.why: The historic bridge spanning the gorge, with spray from the falls drifting over it, is the crossing's icon.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Simien Mountains road near Imet Gogo
places.why: A knife-edge viewpoint over three sides of escarpment is the single most-photographed spot on the Simien circuit.

places.name: White Desert road at the chalk formations
places.why: Wind-eroded chalk rock shaped like mushrooms and icebergs surrounds the desert track after Farafra.

places.name: A104 at the Great Rift Valley viewpoint
places.why: A roadside escarpment stop above Lake Naivasha gives the classic first look down into the Rift.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Road to Merzouga at Erg Chebbi
places.why: The Sahara's tallest Moroccan dunes rise straight from the tarmac's end, the road's classic sunset stop.

places.name: Wild Coast road at Hole in the Wall
places.why: A cliff pierced clean through by the sea is the Wild Coast's best-known and most remote landmark.

places.name: Route du Volcan at Pas de Bellecombe
places.why: The road ends at a crater rim overlooking Piton de la Fournaise's black lava plain and smoking cones.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: RN7 at the Isalo sandstone massif
places.why: Wind-eroded sandstone ridges glow red at sunset beside RN7's most scenic stretch.

places.name: D601 at the Fish River Canyon main viewpoint
places.why: The rim road's main lookout, also called Hell's Bend, gives the classic view down the world's second-largest canyon.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Karakoram Highway at Khunjerab Pass
places.why: The highest paved international border crossing in the world, hemmed by snow peaks on the China–Pakistan frontier.

places.name: Pamir Highway at Ak-Baital Pass
places.why: The highway's highest pass crosses a barren, high-altitude desert plateau near the Chinese border.

places.name: Leh–Manali Highway at Baralacha La
places.why: Glacial lakes and year-round snow patches surround the highway's key pass, closed roughly half the year.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Khardung La road
places.why: One of the world's highest motorable passes, with prayer flags strung across the summit signboard.

places.name: Srinagar–Leh Highway at Zoji La
places.why: A narrow, unfenced shelf road across the pass is Ladakh's main lifeline and its most treacherous stretch.

places.name: Rohtang Pass summit
places.why: The gateway pass between Kullu Valley and Lahaul is snowbound roughly seven months of the year.

places.name: Chang La road to Pangong Tso
places.why: A brilliant blue high-altitude lake stretching to the Tibetan border is Ladakh's most photographed drive destination.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Mount Fuji Skyline at the Fujinomiya 5th Station
places.why: The paved road's terminus at 2,400m gives the closest drive-up view of Fuji's summit crater rim.

places.name: Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route at the Snow Corridor
places.why: Spring ploughing leaves walls of snow up to 20m tall lining the road for weeks each year.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Tianmen Mountain Road (99 Bends)
places.why: 99 numbered hairpins climb 1,100m up a sheer cliff face to Heaven's Gate cave.

places.name: Guoliang Tunnel Road
places.why: A tunnel hand-carved through the cliff by villagers, with irregular window-openings looking straight down the gorge.

places.name: Duku Highway at the Tianshan Grand Canyon
places.why: Red sandstone cliffs and a river gorge line one of the most remote and seasonally shut highways in China.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Ha Giang Loop at Mã Pí Lèng Pass
places.why: A ledge carved into limestone cliffs above the Nho Quế River is the loop's most-photographed stretch.

places.name: Hai Van Pass summit
places.why: Old French bunkers sit at the top of a pass overlooking the South China Sea on both sides of the ridge.

places.name: Mae Hong Son Loop at Pai Canyon
places.why: A narrow eroded ridge trail beside the loop road gives sunset views over the surrounding hills.

places.name: Desert Highway spur into Wadi Rum
places.why: Red sand and towering sandstone jebels either side of the track are Jordan's most iconic desert scene.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: King's Highway above Dana Biosphere Reserve
places.why: The ancient highway skirts the rim of a canyon dropping 1,000m to the Wadi Araba.

places.name: Jebel Hafeet Road
places.why: 60 curves climb a nearly treeless mountain to a summit overlooking the Emirates and Oman.

places.name: Dead Sea Highway near Mount Nebo
places.why: On a clear day the overlook here reaches across the Dead Sea and Jordan Valley to Jerusalem.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Ella–Nuwara Eliya road at the Nine Arch Bridge
places.why: A colonial-era viaduct arcing through tea-plantation jungle is the hill-country road's most-shot stop.

places.name: Georgian Military Highway at the Cross Pass
places.why: The road's ancient highest point, marked by a Soviet mosaic monument, looks over the Caucasus's Devil's Valley.

places.name: Road to Charyn Canyon at the Valley of Castles
places.why: Red sandstone spires eroded into castle shapes line the canyon rim east of Almaty.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Gobi Desert route at Khongoryn Els dunes
places.why: Mongolia's 'singing sands' rise up to 300m from the steppe, the classic stop on any Gobi loop.

places.name: Jeju coastal road at Seongsan Ilchulbong
places.why: A tuff volcanic cone rising straight from the sea is the island's ring-road icon, best at sunrise.

places.name: Taroko Gorge Road at Swallow Grotto
places.why: The marble-walled gorge narrows to a sheer, swallow-nested cliff face right above the road.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Kintamani road above Mount Batur
places.why: A roadside ridge looks straight across the caldera lake to Batur's still-active cone.

places.name: Banaue road at the rice terrace viewpoint
places.why: 2,000-year-old stone terraces climb the mountainside above the road in the Philippines' best-known landscape.

places.name: Jomsom road through the Kali Gandaki gorge
places.why: The world's deepest gorge opens up beside the road between Annapurna and Dhaulagiri.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Thimphu–Punakha Highway at Dochula Pass
places.why: 108 memorial chortens line the pass, with a wall of eastern Himalayan peaks behind them on clear mornings.

places.name: Cappadocia road at Uçhisar Castle
places.why: A carved rock citadel above the fairy-chimney valleys is the region's highest and most-photographed viewpoint.

places.name: Road to Jebel Shams at the Grand Canyon of Oman
places.why: A cliff-edge track reaches a rim overlooking Wadi Nakhr, a 1,000m gorge nicknamed Oman's Grand Canyon.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Munnar road through the Western Ghats
places.why: Terraced tea estates roll over every hillside along this ghat road above Munnar town.

places.name: Thakhek Loop at Kong Lor Cave
places.why: A river cave running 7km through a limestone mountain is the loop's dramatic centrepiece stop.

places.name: Sapa road at O Quy Ho Pass
places.why: Vietnam's longest mountain pass, often shrouded in cloud, links Sapa to the Lai Chau valley below.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: G318 Sichuan–Tibet Highway at Kamba La Pass
places.why: The highway's most photographed pass looks down on the turquoise curve of Yamdrok Lake far below.

places.name: Great Ocean Road at the Twelve Apostles
places.why: Limestone stacks rising from the Southern Ocean are Australia's most photographed coastal landmark.

places.name: Milford Road at Milford Sound / Mitre Peak
places.why: The road's end reveals Mitre Peak rising sheer from the fiord, New Zealand's most reproduced landscape shot.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Great Alpine Road at Mount Hotham
places.why: Australia's highest sealed through-road tops out at a ski-resort summit often closed by snow in winter.

places.name: Gibb River Road at the Cockburn Range
places.why: A red sandstone escarpment glowing at sunset is the outback track's best-known landmark.

places.name: Stuart Highway at the Devils Marbles
places.why: Giant balanced granite boulders scattered across the outback are the highway's classic photo stop.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Red Centre Way at Uluru
places.why: The monolith at sunset, glowing deep red, is the loop's — and the outback's — defining image.

places.name: Savannah Way at Boodjamulla (Lawn Hill) Gorge
places.why: A hidden emerald gorge cutting through the outback is the Savannah Way's most surprising stop.

places.name: Cape York's Old Telegraph Track at Gunshot Creek
places.why: A notoriously steep, rutted creek crossing is the 4x4 track's most photographed and most attempted obstacle.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Eyre Highway at the Bunda Cliffs
places.why: Sheer 80m cliffs dropping straight into the Southern Ocean line the world's longest dead-straight stretch of road.

places.name: Great Eastern Drive at Wineglass Bay
places.why: A perfect curve of white sand seen from the saddle lookout is Tasmania's most photographed beach.

places.name: Crown Range Road summit
places.why: The country's highest main road climbs above the Kawarau Gorge with the Southern Alps on the horizon.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Skippers Canyon Road
places.why: A one-lane gravel shelf blasted into a gorge wall above the Shotover River, still rated among the world's most dangerous.

places.name: State Highway 6 at Pancake Rocks
places.why: Stacked limestone layers with blowholes erupting at high tide are the West Coast road's must-stop.

places.name: Southern Scenic Route at Nugget Point
places.why: A slender lighthouse headland looking over rock stacks called The Nuggets is the route's iconic end point.

places.name: Coromandel Loop Road near Cathedral Cove
places.why: A sea-carved rock archway framing a hidden beach is the peninsula's most photographed stop.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Queens Road along the Coral Coast
places.why: Fringing reef visible just offshore lines Viti Levu's main coastal highway.

places.name: Captain Cook Highway at Rex Lookout
places.why: Rainforest-covered mountains meet the reef-fringed coast at this cliffside lookout north of Cairns.

places.name: Arthur's Pass Road summit
places.why: The road's viaduct and summit lookout cross the Southern Alps' most dramatic gap, occasionally closed by snow or slips.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: US 101 Oregon Coast at Thor's Well
places.why: A hole in the basalt shelf that seems to drain the ocean is the coast highway's strangest, most-shot stop.

places.name: Teton Park Road at Snake River Overlook
places.why: The Ansel Adams view of the Tetons over a bend in the Snake River is the park road's classic frame.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Serra do Rio do Rastro switchbacks
places.why: Nine stacked hairpins drop 1,000m off the plateau in a few kilometres, Brazil's most-photographed mountain road.

places.name: Ruta 225 at the Petrohué viewpoint
places.why: Turquoise rapids frame the perfect cone of Osorno Volcano from a pull-off on the Lake District road.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Snæfellsnes Peninsula road at Kirkjufell
places.why: A cone-shaped mountain beside a small waterfall is Iceland's most photographed non-Ring-Road stop.

places.name: A830 Road to the Isles at the Glenfinnan Viaduct
places.why: A curved railway viaduct above the road, made famous on screen, is the route's best-known pull-off view.

places.name: Durmitor Ring Road at Black Lake
places.why: A glacial lake beneath Durmitor's peaks is the ring road's centrepiece stop in Montenegro's highest range.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: SH8 at Llogara Pass
places.why: The coast road's mountain crossing drops abruptly to the Ionian Sea, Albania's most dramatic viewpoint.

places.name: Coastal road at Legzira Beach
places.why: Twin natural rock arches on an open Atlantic beach are the southern coast road's signature stop.

places.name: Ngorongoro Crater rim road
places.why: The rim road looks straight down 600m into an intact volcanic caldera crowded with wildlife.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Route 90 at the Masada viewpoint
places.why: A clifftop fortress ruin above the Dead Sea's shrinking shoreline is the highway's best-known stop.

places.name: Shimanami Kaido at the Kurushima-Kaikyo Bridge
places.why: A chain of suspension bridges strung between islands makes this crossing Japan's most photographed drive-and-cycle route.

places.name: Cameron Highlands road above the tea estates
places.why: Rolling green tea terraces climb every hillside along this cool-climate mountain road.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Spiti Valley road at Kunzum La
places.why: A high desert pass strung with prayer flags marks the boundary between Lahaul and Spiti's moonscape.

places.name: Lindis Pass summit
places.why: Tussock-covered golden hills roll away from the road's high point between the Mackenzie Basin and Central Otago.

places.name: Flinders Chase road at Remarkable Rocks
places.why: Wind- and salt-sculpted granite boulders balanced on a coastal dome are the island's most photographed stop.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime

places.name: Ring Road spur to Vestrahorn
places.why: Jagged peaks reflected in black-sand tidal flats make this detour off Route 1 one of Iceland's most-shot views.

places.name: Ring Road at Skógafoss
places.why: A 60m waterfall visible from the highway itself is one of the Ring Road's most-stopped-for sights.
places.source: National Geographic Drives of a Lifetime
